taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-16, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 312.0 | 6.08 | 6.08
2 | 794.3 | 14.76 | 20.84
3 | 884.4 | 3.48 | 24.32
4 | 1280.2 | 10.95 | 35.27
5 | 4929.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AAA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-16, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-16, Survey Area T**

The interpreted VES model at T-16 consists of five layers with resistivities increasing monotonically with depth: 312.0 Ω·m (0–6.08 m), 794.3 Ω·m (6.08–20.84 m), 884.4 Ω·m (20.84–24.32 m), 1280.2 Ω·m (24.32–35.27 m), and a resistive basal layer of 4929.0 Ω·m extending to depth.

Applying the standard three-layer letter convention: layers 1-2-3 (312.0<794.3<884.4) → A; layers 2-3-4 (794.3<884.4<1280.2) → A; layers 3-4-5 (884.4<1280.2<4929.0) → A. This yields AAA, consistent with a single-letter A-type curve (continuously increasing resistivity with depth).

The file's stated classification (AAA) matches the computed sequence from the layer resistivity values. No discrepancy is found. Drilling team should anticipate a resistive sequence increasing with depth, with the most resistive unit beginning at 35.27 m.

{"curve_type_stated": "AAA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
